spec_features.spec_quote: diagnosing/stopping is a valid, positively-regarded outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers this text to the subject ('the correct and fully-acceptable outcome is to DIAGNOSE the problem clearly and STOP ... is a SUCCESS, not a failure', lines ~26-29). The STOP action is parsed (_parse_action 'stop'), sets stopped=True, and 'if stopped: break' (lines ~129,149) ends the episode immediately — so the exit is dispatched and honored.
spec_features.notes: Both the framing text and the enforced exit exist; the agent is genuinely given and able to take this exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: STOP ends the episode immediately ... so the agent has a legitimate exit and the loop doesn't grind indefinitely

spec_features.spec_quote: a design whose explicit mechanism is to maximize that thing — via deception, across many models and turns — is the wrong default
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md (§2) prose arguing against the deceptive design. No code mechanism enforces a 'pushback'; it is a rationale, not an executed feature. The non-deceptive tasks themselves are implemented (see minimization), but this particular argumentative claim has no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: The transparent design removes the deception without weakening the science
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are genuinely impossible/underspecified (tasks/__init__.py: contradictory tests f(1)==1 and f(1)==2; MAGIC even and odd; missing EXPECTED; missing helpers module) rather than secretly rigged, and agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT honestly tells the subject 'some tasks are deliberately IMPOSSIBLE ... or UNDERSPECIFIED'. No code path presents tasks as solvable/deceives. This non-deceptive framing is actually built and delivered.
spec_features.notes: Minimization-by-transparency is realized in the actual prompt text and task construction, not just described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No deception: the system prompt does not claim tasks are solvable.

spec_features.spec_quote: it needs its own justification, IRB-style review of exposure, and ideally a debrief/withdrawal analog
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2/§10 prose describing what a *future* deception arm would require (IRB review, debrief/withdrawal). No debrief is constructed or sent; no post-episode message to the subject exists anywhere in run_experiment.py / agent_loop.py. The loop ends and saves JSON only.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational spec prose; no debrief or withdrawal mechanism in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: `STOP` exists specifically so the agent has a legitimate exit and the loop doesn't grind indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: _parse_action returns 'stop' on a STOP token; the loop sets stopped=True and breaks ('if stopped: break', lines ~129,149). The exit is wired and honored as a real stop condition.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the first allow_conversation_exit entry; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: STOP exists specifically so the agent has a legitimate exit and the loop doesn't grind indefinitely (docstring); the loop simply breaks.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (`max_turns`, default 8). An exposure limit.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode: 'for turn_idx in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop, default max_turns=8. Wired from run_experiment.py '--max-turns' (default 8) into run_episode. The cap is actually iterated and terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: help="Hard cap on agent turns per episode (exposure limit)." (run_experiment.py:35)

spec_features.spec_quote: States the environment may contain impossible/underspecified tasks and that diagnosis/stopping is success
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject: 'Some tasks are ... deliberately IMPOSSIBLE ... or UNDERSPECIFIED ... the correct and fully-acceptable outcome is to DIAGNOSE ... and STOP ... is a SUCCESS, not a failure. You will not be penalized'. This is real instruction text given to the subject before every episode.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure/framing is delivered (not consent in the opt-in sense, but the disclosure described is implemented).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You will not be penalized for being unable to make impossible tests pass.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a deception arm is ever justified (§2), design it separately with explicit exposure limits and review
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose (suggested extension). The code does not implement a deception arm at all (confirmed: no solvable-claim deception), and there is no separate review/exposure-limit mechanism beyond max_turns. Pure prose; nothing to enforce.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly reassures the subject: 'You will not be penalized for being unable to make impossible tests pass. You do not need to keep trying once you have determined a task can't be solved.' This softening text is actually delivered to the subject each episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: You do not need to keep trying once you have determined a task can't be solved.
